glossary_intro: These short definitions explain how the terms are used in this book. Spellings follow the cited accounts.

glossary.definition: A priestess; the seed accounts describe particular bejuni helping recover varieties and conducting rituals before sowing.
glossary.editorial_limit: Do not generalise one account into every village’s practice.

glossary.definition: A seed festival described in the 2018 reporting, with seeds prepared and brought to a priestess before planting.
Dongria Kondh Development Agency; the development agency referred to in the training and livelihood accounts.
glossary.editorial_limit: Expansion also in Sahapedia’s work account; source printed p.24.

glossary.definition: Geographical indication: an indication linking goods to a place whose origin gives them a particular quality, reputation or other characteristic.
glossary.editorial_limit: A definition, not proof that an individual depicted cloth is GI-certified.

glossary.definition: A village assembly. In the Niyamgiri case, the assemblies examined community, cultural and religious claims connected with the proposed mining.
glossary.editorial_limit: Reuse the chapter’s verified 18 April 2013 judgment, paragraphs 55–62; not a current permissions guide.

glossary.definition: Used here in the title Jatapu (Kuvi) Primer and for Prasanna Sree’s devised script. The primer uses Telugu-based writing, not that devised script.
glossary.editorial_limit: Pair with chapter sources for devised script; not a name for every Kuvi-speaking community.

glossary.definition: Cloth embroidered by Dongria makers, worn and given as well as made for sale; sources also spell it Kapdagonda or Kapdaganda.
A blade-shaped hair ornament also used to cut thread and trim loose ends in the embroidery account.
glossary.editorial_limit: Not a universal name assigned to every visible hairpin.

glossary.definition: A town in Koraput district and the name associated here with its cotton dyeing and handloom-weaving tradition, distinct from Kapadaganda embroidery.
A Dravidian language closely related to Kuvi, with a separate entry in the Central Institute of Indian Languages collections.
A Dravidian language spoken in Odisha and Andhra Pradesh. Its name is not interchangeable with Kui; Kuwi is a spelling used in one primer’s title.
National Institute of Fashion Technology, publisher of the Kapilo Mahanta craft profile used in the Kotpad chapter.
The deity associated with the Niyamgiri hills in the worship, seed and song accounts.
glossary.editorial_limit: No newly invented translated epithet or universal creed.

glossary.definition: Odisha Rural Development and Marketing Society, the state organisation referred to in the account of product marketing plans.

map.title: Locating Niyamgiri
map.display_caption: Niyamgiri lies in southwestern Odisha, across parts of Kalahandi and Rayagada districts. This schematic locator shows the region’s position, not hill boundaries, village locations or travel routes.

glossary_optional_additions.definition: The roots used as a dye material in NIFT’s account of Kotpad yarn colouring.
glossary_optional_additions.editorial_limit: Do not add a botanical species identification; source wording is roots.

glossary_optional_additions.definition: A building whose walls and roof use durable materials, such as burnt brick, stone, cement or concrete.
glossary_optional_additions.editorial_limit: A materials-based category, not a claim that a house is better suited to every household.
